scenario.name: CosmicStrand Motherboard SPI Flash UEFI Rootkit (CSMCORE -> ntoskrnl.exe Chain)
scenario.overview: Imagine a saboteur who does not break into a bank lobby at all, but instead carves a hidden mechanical detour directly into the stone foundation chip poured beneath the building. Even if the owners demolish every floor and replace every safe inside, the stone foundation still triggers a three-person baton relay every morning at sunrise, switching off the building alarm clock before the bank governor even takes a single step. In this scenario (T1542.001, CosmicStrand Motherboard SPI Flash UEFI Rootkit (CSMCORE -> ntoskrnl.exe Chain)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: motherboard SPI Flash Infection of CSMCORE, then multi-Hop Boot Hooking Relay, then patchGuard Neutralization, ntoskrnl.exe. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Motherboard SPI Flash Infection of CSMCORE, then Multi-Hop Boot Hooking Relay, then PatchGuard Neutralization, ntoskrnl.exe, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Motherboard SPI Flash Infection of CSMCORE DXE Driver (HandleProtocol Hook)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1542.001 - System Firmware)
stages.description: Deep beneath the building floor, the saboteur chisels a secret trigger straight into the permanent stone foundation block that wakes up first every morning. Because that block lives outside the replaceable floors and storage rooms, tearing out every hard drive in the building never removes the trap. CosmicStrand modified the UEFI firmware image stored inside the motherboard’s physical 8MB SPI NOR flash chip, specifically patching the CSMCORE DXE driver (GUID {A062CF1F-8473-4AA3-8793-600BC4FFE9A8}). When the UEFI Driver Execution Environment (DXE) loaded CSMCORE, the patched entry point jumped to shellcode appended in the .reloc section, which hooked EFI_BOOT_SERVICES.HandleProtocol (the core UEFI Boot Service function invoked later when locating and loading the OS boot manager). Because the infection resides entirely inside the motherboard’s SPI flash chip, replacing the SSD/NVMe drive or reinstalling Windows from a clean ISO has zero effect on the rootkit. In the documented EDR exchange from CosmicStrand C2 Server to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ALERT T1542.001 (confirming that the Stage 1: Motherboard SPI Flash Infection of CSMCORE DXE Driver (HandleProtocol Hook) request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: Multi-Hop Boot Hooking Relay (bootmgfw.efi -> winload.efi)). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: Motherboard SPI Flash Infection of CSMCORE DXE Driver (HandleProtocol Hook) / ⇠#1 ALERT T1542.001) from Node ① (#1 CosmicStrand C2 Server) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Patched ntoskrnl.exe & Kernel Implant).

stages.title: Stage 2: Multi-Hop Boot Hooking Relay (bootmgfw.efi -> winload.efi)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1542.003 - Bootkit Hooking Relay)
stages.description: As dawn breaks, the foundation trap passes a hidden baton up a three-stage hallway relay: first catching the front-gate opener as it unlocks the lobby, then tagging the floor-captain loader as it prepares the main hall, making sure the trap rides all the way up to the governor desk. When HandleProtocol was called during boot, CosmicStrand scanned memory for bootmgfw.efi and placed an inline hook on Archpx64TransferTo64BitApplicationAsm. When bootmgfw.efi loaded winload.efi into RAM and called that function, the hook scanned winload.efi for the byte signature of OslArchTransferToKernel (the final OS loader routine that switches the CPU into kernel execution and jumps to ntoskrnl.exe’s entry point) and hooked it in memory. Because bootmgfw.efi, winload.efi, and ntoskrnl.exe on the disk partition are never modified on disk, offline disk forensics and file-hash checks report 100% clean Microsoft system binaries. In the documented EDR exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Motherboard SPI Flash (CSMCORE DXE), Motherboard SPI Flash (CSMCORE DXE) responds with ALERT T1542.003 (confirming that the Stage 2: Multi-Hop Boot Hooking Relay (bootmgfw.efi -> winload.efi) request succeeded on Motherboard SPI Flash (CSMCORE DXE) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: PatchGuard Neutralization, ntoskrnl.exe ZwCreateSection Hook & Kernel C2). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: Multi-Hop Boot Hooking Relay (bootmgfw.efi -> winload.efi) / ⇠#2 ALERT T1542.003) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Motherboard SPI Flash (CSMCORE DXE)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Patched ntoskrnl.exe & Kernel Implant).

stages.title: Stage 3: PatchGuard Neutralization, ntoskrnl.exe ZwCreateSection Hook & Kernel C2
stages.subtitle: Command and Control & Privilege Escalation (T1014 - Rootkit)
stages.description:
One heartbeat before the bank governor opens his eyes, the baton carrier unhooks the master watchdog bell so nobody notices tampered blueprints, plants a secret listener on the room-opening ledger, and opens a hidden courier line straight from the governor private study. At the OslArchTransferToKernel handoff, before ntoskrnl.exe even executed its first instruction, CosmicStrand patched KiFilterFiberContext in ntoskrnl.exe RAM to immediately return (preventing Windows Kernel Patch Protection / PatchGuard from initializing), copied its shellcode into unused .text section slack space inside ntoskrnl.exe, and placed an inline hook on ZwCreateSection (waiting for smss.exe to map KnownDlls
tdll.dll as a signal that the OS network stack is ready before mapping its final kernel-mode C2 implant). Once Windows networking initialized, the kernel implant resolved its C2 domain via raw kernel sockets (tdi.sys) to fetch second-stage user/kernel payloads. In the documented EDR exchange from Motherboard SPI Flash (CSMCORE DXE) to Boot Chain (bootmgfw -> winload.efi), Boot Chain (bootmgfw -> winload.efi) responds with ALERT T1014 (confirming that the Stage 3: PatchGuard Neutralization, ntoskrnl.exe ZwCreateSection Hook & Kernel C2 request succeeded on Boot Chain (bootmgfw -> winload.efi) and completing the final execution objective of CosmicStrand Motherboard SPI Flash UEFI Rootkit (CSMCORE -> ntoskrnl.exe Chain)). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: PatchGuard Neutralization, ntoskrnl.exe ZwCreateSection Hook & Kernel C2 / ⇠#3 ALERT T1014) from Node ③ (#3 Motherboard SPI Flash (CSMCORE DXE)) to Node ④ (#4 Boot Chain (bootmgfw -> winload.efi)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Patched ntoskrnl.exe & Kernel Implant).
